newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF to discuss Dec/Jan data, 1997 plans in Moscow.
newsitem.headline: IMF to discuss Dec/Jan data, 1997 plans in Moscow.

text.p: International Monetary Fund experts are due to arrive in Moscow on Tuesday for a regular monitoring mission and will also discuss a detailed economic programme for 1997, an IMF official said.

Chief representative Thomas Wolf told Reuters the delegation would look at Russia's economic performance in December and the first half of January. The experts were likely to stay in Moscow for about 10 days.
They would also discuss Russia's economic plans for 1997, focusing on macroeconomic targets as well as on priorities for structural reform.
"Last year we ended up with a range of sectors to be addressed, but the structural emphasis for this year will be a little bit more focused," Wolf said.
The IMF last year approved a three-year $10 billion loan for Russia but detailed plans must be drawn up each year before the funds can be paid out.
Wolf said it was not yet clear if a statement of intent would be agreed during this visit or if any statement would be made public.

Russia won praise from the IMF last year for its strong performance in bringing inflation down, but structural reforms have been slow, stalled in the first half by expensive promises during the presidential election campaign and in the second half by re-elected President Boris Yeltsin's protracted illness.
The president fell ill again earlier this month and he is being treated for pneumonia in Moscow's elite Central Clinical Hospital.

The government has promised to keep inflation under one percent a month this year. Consumer prices rose 21.8 percent in the year to December, down sharply from 131 percent in the year to December 1995.
